newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures end lower, extend slide.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures end lower, extend slide.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Friday, continuing their slide this week on waning cooling demand and ample, cheap hydroelectricity supply in the western U.S., industry sources said.
"Things keep on coming off. We haven't seen a bottom yet," said one Houston trader.
"It looks a whole lot weaker," echoed another trader.
Today's price increase by Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) for its daily power products failed to lift the market higher against earlier market expectations.
BPA hiked values for daily surplus power during heavy load hours on Monday by one to three dollars to as high as $20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
"Even BPA can't sell if someone could undercut them, and if demand continues to fall," said the first trader.
October California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled at $15.42 per MWh, down 43 cents after traded between $15.25 and $15.90.
November COB finished down one cent at $16.32 after hitting a session low of $16.10. Active deferred COB months ended mixed.
October Palo Verde (PV) futures settled at $15.85 per MWh, down 36 cents after bouncing between $15.80 and $16.20.
November PV finished down 25 cents at $14.90, its Friday session low. Outer PV contracts ended flat to lower.
Brokers and traders pegged short-term support for October COB at $15.10-$15.30 range and October PV in the $15.50 area.
In the next six to 10 days, the West was expected to experience mostly cooler-than-normal weather.
NYMEX estimated 275 COB and 269 PV contracts were sold.
